draft.title: Fairness in the justice system
card: In the VCE study design, fairness is about the processes used to reach an outcome. It does not mean everyone gets the result they want.
the person or body deciding the case is impartial and free from outside influence, such as pressure from the government or a party.
each party has a chance to know the case against them and the evidence behind it, so they can prepare a response.
each party has a chance to present their side, to question the other side's evidence, and to be heard before a decision is made.
draft.remember: A fair process is impartial, open about the case and lets each side be heard.

a.q: Which of these best shows fairness in the justice system?
opts: A judge with no link to either party hears the case
Both parties get the same outcome in the case
The accused is told the verdict before the hearing
The most serious charges are always heard first
a.why: Fairness is about the process, and an impartial judge is part of an independent decision-maker. Getting the same outcome is the tempting option, but fairness does not guarantee any particular result.
a.clue: Fairness looks at how a decision is reached, not what it is.

b.q: Before her hearing, Priya is given none of the evidence the prosecution will use against her. Which element of fairness is most directly missing?
opts: A chance to know the case against her
A chance to question the other side's evidence
A lighter sentence than other offenders receive
b.why: Priya has not been given the evidence, so she cannot prepare a response. Questioning evidence at the hearing is related, but the missing step here is knowing the case beforehand.
b.clue: What does she need to have before the hearing begins?

a.best: A judge with no link to either party hears the case

b.best: A chance to know the case against her
